Beállítom Elfogtak és kihallgattak a rendőrök egy 17 éves budapesti fiatalt, aki péntek este bombafenyegetést tett egy budapesti iskola ellen – közölte szombaton a Budapesti Rendőr-főkapitányság. Közleményük szerint a fiatal péntek este nyolc óra után pár perccel hívta fel a 112-es segélyhívót, és eltorzított hangon közölte, hogy bomba van egy budapesti tanintézményben. Az üres iskolát a Készenléti Rendőrség Tűzszerész Szolgálata átvizsgálta, ott semmilyen robbanóanyagot, vagy robbantásra alkalmas szerkezetet nem találtak. A rendőrök közben azonosították, hogy a hívás egy zuglói nyilvános telefonfülkéből érkezett, amelynek közelében néhány fiatalt igazoltattak. Hamar kiderült, hogy a 112-t korábban a társaság egyik tagja hívta, akit végül XIV. kerületi otthonában fogtak el. A zuglói nyomozók a 17 éves fiút közveszéllyel fenyegetés bűntett miatt hallgatták ki, és elismerte, hogy ő volt a telefonáló. Fenyegető hívását azzal indokolta, hogy az általa megjelölt intézménybe olyan fiatalok járnak, akik gúnyolták, ezért haragudott rájuk. Tettét megbánta. Szerda este a Budapest XV. kerületében lévő Kontyfa Általános Iskola és Gimnázium, valamint a Pestújhelyi Általános Iskola kapott bombafenyegetéseket. A 24.hu pedig arról számolt be , hogy szerda délelőtt bombariadó volt a XVIII. kerületi Eötvös Loránd általános iskolában, ahonnan mindenkit hazaküldtek. Composite: Reuters/Pool EPA/AP Ukraine Explainer Trump, Musk, Zelenskyy: who is blaming who in the Ukraine-Starlink row? A war of words has erupted over who is responsible for the restrictions on Starshield access in Ukraine Jonathan Yerushalmy Thu 22 Oct 2026 22.16 EDT Last modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 22.17 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A war of words has erupted between the Trump administration , officials in Kyiv and Elon Musk over who is to blame for limiting Ukraine’s access to Space X’s military-grade version of Starlink. The restrictions to Starshield have rendered many of the drones used by Kyiv to strike behind the frontlines inoperable and hampered air defence systems that stop Russian attacks, according to Ukrainian officials . What is Starshield, SpaceX’s military-grade Starlink system, and how will its restriction affect Ukraine? Read more Donald Trump said on Thursday that the service was running again at full speed, but a European official speaking to the Associated Press denied the service was fully functioning. Amid the diplomatic handwringing, civilian casualties in Ukraine have surged , and the question over who is ultimately responsible for limiting Kyiv’s access has remained unanswered. 1. Donald Trump The restrictions came as relations between the US and Ukraine hit their lowest point since Russia’s full-scale invasion nearly five years ago. Donald Trump has accused Ukraine of driving up diesel costs for Americans through its attacks on Russian oil refineries. Analysis by the BBC found that the US-Israel war on Iran and resulting restrictions on oil exports from the Gulf have likely had a greater impact on global diesel supplies. Trump initially denied any responsibility for the changes to Starshield, telling reporters last Friday: “I don’t know if it was anybody, but it wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon,” referring to Musk, SpaceX’s CEO. Trump’s cabinet backed him up, with secretary of state Marco Rubio saying on Wednesday: “What I can tell you with certainty is the president of the United States nor anyone in our system ever requested that any changes to that system be made.” Rubio, however, also made a comment that threw suspicion on to Musk, the world’s richest man. The president has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr Musk. That’s a private company. The president doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything. Ukraine war briefing: Uncertainty over Kyiv’s Starlink access after Trump claims Musk restored service Read more The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that the US president had asked Musk to restore the service, with Trump later telling reporters the system was “back”. He refused to comment on whether he had spoken to Musk, but appeared to suggest the ultimate power to limit the service rested with the SpaceX CEO. “I guess the bottom line, he put it back,” Trump said, referring to Musk. However, John Cornyn, a Republican who is in his final weeks as the US senator for Texas, told US media that he didn’t believe Musk would have acted “without at least the acquiescence of the White House”. 2. Elon Musk Musk has supported Trump’s calls for Volodymyr Zelenskyy to be replaced and has been highly critical of the Ukrainian president. However, he was quick to blame the limits on Starshield on the Trump administration, writing on X last week that the systems were “owned and controlled by the US government”. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS. Musk – one of the Republican party’s biggest donors and a Trump ally – continued to deny responsibility for the changes. However, on Tuesday the Wall Street Journal reported that Musk made the order to slow down Starshield, with the paper’s sources in disagreement over whether this was made in concert with Trump. Vice-president JD Vance backed Musk on Thursday, saying the billionaire “doesn’t want to get in the middle of what is a war between two state actors without the United States government effectively directing him on what to do”. So I don’t think this is about Elon. I think it’s fundamentally what is America’s policy in Ukraine and Russia going to be. 3. Volodymyr Zelenskyy The Ukrainian president initially blamed the restrictions on “SpaceX and the United States”, saying on Wednesday last week that the move would “bring a lot of human losses … of course, people will die”. Shortly after the systems failed, Zelenskyy said there were no similar restrictions on Starshield terminals in European Union countries and that they applied only to Ukraine. “In other words, this is a planned operation.” Zelenskyy said at the weekend that Musk’s SpaceX was ultimately responsible for suddenly limiting the speed at which Starshield worked in Ukraine. “It was a message from [the] American government to limit the speed ... And technically, SpaceX did it.” Despite Trump’s insistence on Thursday that the service had resumed, a senior European official told the Associated Press that nothing had changed in the operation of Starshield. Prior to Trump’s comments, Zelenskyy ⁠said full Starshield speed had still not ⁠been restored ⁠for Ukraine, ​adding that he hoped for talks ⁠with Rubio in the ⁠coming days.
